_about: Single source of truth for every rendering, and the auditable term ledger (check 5). ONE rendering per referent for the whole book. Japanese names in Hepburn with macrons; conventional English forms for well-known figures (Nobunaga, Hideyoshi, Ieyasu). status per entry: 'attested' (form used in English scholarship), 'provisional' (romanization mine, not found outside), 'decided' (a project style call). The 'pinyin' field holds the romaji reading. Principal cast carry principal:true with a cast one-liner and cast_order.

葛籠重蔵.cast: The Iga ninja whose family was slaughtered in Nobunaga's invasion; hired for one last impossible commission, the assassination of Hideyoshi.
葛籠重蔵.note: 葛籠 is glossed つづら (Tsuzura) in the text; given name 重蔵 Jūzō. Referred to in narration as 重蔵.

重蔵.note: Bare given name of Tsuzura Jūzō, used throughout the narration.

風間五平.cast: Jūzō's fellow disciple under Jirōzaemon, beautiful and detached; abandoned the shadow arts to climb in the new order, and is set against Jūzō.
風間五平.note: 風間 glossed かざま (Kazama); 五平 Gohei.

五平.note: Bare given name of Kazama Gohei.

下柘植次郎左衛門.cast: The disfigured old master of Iga, a former ninja captain who harried Nobunaga's armies in the Iga Rebellion; Kisaru's father, and teacher of both Jūzō and Gohei.
下柘植次郎左衛門.note: 下柘植 glossed しもつげ (Shimotsuge). In the opening he is 老人, 'the old man'.

次郎左衛門.note: Bare name of Shimotsuge Jirōzaemon in narration; also styled 'the old man' / 'the Master' where the source uses 老人 / お師匠.

木猿.cast: Jirōzaemon's fierce, unreadable daughter, betrothed to Gohei; she means to learn Gohei's fate herself.
木猿.note: Written 木さる in the ch04 title; 木猿 here. Her father wishes she had been a son.

黒阿弥.cast: Jūzō's aged genin, under five shaku tall with a face like a boy's, who has served the Tsuzura since Jūzō's father's day.
黒阿弥.note: Full form 佐那具ノ黒阿弥, Sanagu-no-Kuroami.

織田信長.note: The warlord whose 1581 invasion destroyed Iga; killed at the Honnō-ji in 1582.

豊臣秀吉.note: Ruler of Japan by 1591; the assassination target of the novel.

家康.note: Tokugawa Ieyasu; crossed Iga in 1582 fleeing the Honnō-ji Incident.

惟任日向守光秀.note: Akechi Mitsuhide, who killed Nobunaga at the Honnō-ji; here under the name and court title Nobunaga had granted him.

丹羽長秀.note: Oda commander on the Yamashiro road in the 1581 invasion; his HQ at Ōyado is the target of the fire-raid.

滝川勝雄.note: Commander of Maruyama Castle in the novel; reading of 勝雄 not independently confirmed.

信雄.note: Oda Nobunaga's son, adopted into the Kitabatake house of Ise; led the failed first Iga campaign.

柘植清広.note: Also 柘植太郎清広. Named leader of the Iga league in the novel.

百地新之丞.note: An Iga gōshi of Tatsunokuchi, of the Momochi band.

楯岡ノ道順.note: Legendary Iga jōnin (a.k.a. Momochi Sandayū); commander of the hundred-man shinobi corps.

葛籠太郎兵衛.note: Jūzō's ailing father, killed in the invasion.

今井宗久.note: Sakai merchant and tea master high in Hideyoshi's favor; the secret paymaster of the plot.

千宗易.note: Sen no Rikyū, the great tea master; here under his lay name Sōeki.

音羽ノ城戸.note: Iga genin; historically the marksman who ambushed Nobunaga at the Aekuni Shrine.

松永久秀/弾正久秀/久秀.note: The warlord who burned the Tōdai-ji Great Buddha in 1567; 弾正 (Danjō) is his court title. Died 1577.

松倉蔵人/蔵人.note: The scarred leader in the Aizen-dō, who claims to be a rōnin of the Shibata house; Jūzō takes him for a broken Mino bandit and kills him. 蔵人 doubles as a court-office name, hence Jūzō's mockery.

雲兵衛.note: The young ex-sailor and one-time balladeer in Matsukura's band; Jūzō spares and conscripts him.

懸巣ノ次郎.note: Matsukura's foster-retainer, found stabbed dead beneath the Great Buddha. 懸巣 = a jay.

小萩.note: The taciturn Nara courtesan who is in fact Imai Sōkyū's guide-agent, sent to meet Jūzō; a Kōga woman, Jūzō suspects.

武田勝頼.note: Last lord of the Takeda of Kai; destroyed by Nobunaga and Ieyasu in 1582.

伊勢屋嘉兵衛.note: The Kyōto shopkeeper's cover identity Jūzō assigns to Kuroami at the end of ch01.

三好三人衆.note: The three Miyoshi captains who contested control of the Kinai after 1564; Matsunaga's war with them burned the Great Buddha.

伊賀.note: The 'hidden country', home province of the ninja.

甲賀.note: The neighbouring ninja district in Ōmi.

御斎峠.note: 御斎峠 (usually Otodo-tōge) is glossed おとぎとうげ in the text, matching the chapter title おとぎ峠; site of Jūzō's grandfather's hermitage.

大屋戸.note: Crossroads hamlet north of Kashiwara; Niwa Nagahide's HQ in 1581.

柏原.note: Site of the Iga gōshi's last-stand fort in 1581.

堺.note: The merchant port; home of Imai Sōkyū.

敢国神社.note: The ichinomiya (first shrine) of Iga province.

東大寺.note: The great Nara temple; its colossal bronze Vairocana is the 'rain-soaked Buddha' of the chapter.

二月堂.note: The Hall of the Second Month at Tōdai-ji.

油坂.note: A slope on the eastern edge of Nara where Jūzō takes an inn.

飛火野.note: A meadow in the Kasuga precinct of Nara.

駿河.note: Coastal province east of Kai; on the Tōkaidō.

呂宋.note: The northern Philippines, newly under Spanish rule from Manila.

愛染堂.note: A hall of Aizen Myō-ō in the ruined Tōdai-ji cloister; the scene of the killing.

多聞院.note: A cloister of Kōfuku-ji whose diary, the Tamon-in nikki, records the 1567 fire.

乱波.note: A Kantō term for a shinobi/spy; used interchangeably with 忍び in the text.

伊賀ノ乱.note: The Tenshō Iga War; Nobunaga's 1581 invasion (Tenshō 9).

当薬.note: The dried herb Swertia japonica, a bitter folk stomach remedy.

愛染明王.note: The 'wisdom king' of passion, Rāgarāja; a patron of love.

毘廬遮那仏.note: The cosmic Buddha; the Tōdai-ji colossus is a Vairocana.
